title_guess: Scheduled vs non-scheduled banks and the types of banks in India

segments.teaches: the RBI Act of 1934 split banks into scheduled and non-scheduled; the RBI began work in 1935

elements.what: thin blue horizontal line across the frame with tick marks for 1934 and 1935
green law-book icon labelled as the 1934 Act, with a drop arrow onto 1934
RBI emblem (gold coin style) with the letters RBI under 1935
bank building under 1934
bank splits into Un-Scheduled (red elbow) and Scheduled (green elbow)

segments.notes: Red vs green colour-coding for the two bank types runs through the video.

segments.teaches: scheduled banks are those listed in the Act's Second Schedule; they must meet criteria (paid-up capital and reserves, liquidity and solvency), and the RBI changes these criteria with economic conditions

elements.what: lined document stack labelled Schedule II beside the law-book
CRITERIA box with two square-bullet lines in blue
dotted elbow arrow from Schedule II down to Scheduled Banks
light-blue fill over the criteria box
note under a black rule: criteria keep changing with conditions
dotted elbow arrow labelled 'Change' from the RBI emblem up to the criteria box

segments.notes: Dotted elbow connectors tie a document to its consequences across the timeline.

segments.teaches: scheduled banks can borrow cheap credit from the RBI for normal needs; non-scheduled banks can borrow only in emergencies

elements.what: RBI emblem at the top with an elbow connector down
bank building with red and green branches
vertical green banknote labelled Loan on the arrow from RBI to Scheduled Banks
blue paragraph under each bank type
yellow highlight on the 'emergency or abnormal circumstances' phrase

segments.notes: Banknote placed on the arrow itself shows money flowing down.

segments.teaches: non-scheduled banks pay a higher rate when they borrow; scheduled status also brings credibility and reputation

elements.what: second Loan banknote on a new arrow to the Un-Scheduled side
red % on the left, green % on the right, with a big > between them at the RBI fork
yellow band on the Scheduled Banks label
row of five gold stars
caption beside the stars: enhanced credibility and reputation

segments.notes: Rate comparison drawn as two coloured % signs and a > symbol, no numbers.

segments.teaches: both groups contain commercial banks and co-operative banks

elements.what: bank building moved to top centre
bank -> Un-Scheduled / Scheduled -> each splits into Commercial Banks and Co-operative Banks with thin green elbow arrows

segments.notes: Bank icon and its two branches carry over and move up; the tree grows downward.

segments.teaches: scheduled commercial banks include public, private, foreign, regional rural, small finance and payments banks; non-scheduled commercial include private, foreign, small finance, payments and local area banks

elements.what: dotted vertical stems under each Commercial Banks node with leaf items added one at a time
tiny curved green arrows pointing to each leaf item

segments.notes: Leaves appear about 1.5 s apart, right side first (6 items), then left side (5 items). A yellow promo strip replaces the bottom banner near the end.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels with app-store badges faded in
